question: After placing an intrauterine balloon and inflating it with 300–500 mL of saline for atonic PPH, you observe that there is no ongoing bleeding around or through the balloon. This is best described as:

answers.text: An indication to remove the balloon immediately and switch to surgical management

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. No ongoing bleeding after balloon inflation indicates the tamponade has SUCCEEDED (positive tamponade test). Immediate removal and surgery would be inappropriate at this point.

answers.text: A positive tamponade test — indicating balloon tamponade is likely sufficient and surgery may be avoided

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. A positive tamponade test (no ongoing bleeding with balloon inflated) means mechanical compression is sufficient to arrest haemorrhage. Leave the balloon in situ for 24–48 hours under antibiotic cover, gradually deflating before removal.

answers.text: A negative tamponade test — confirming ongoing coagulopathy requiring fresh frozen plasma

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. A negative tamponade test would mean ongoing bleeding DESPITE balloon inflation, suggesting the mechanism is not amenable to tamponade alone (e.g., coagulopathy, structural tear). No bleeding = positive test = tamponade working.

answers.text: Proof that the original diagnosis of uterine atony was incorrect

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Successful balloon tamponade is entirely consistent with uterine atony as the cause of PPH. It simply confirms that mechanical compression is sufficient to achieve haemostasis.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: no bleeding after balloon inflation = POSITIVE tamponade test (tamponade is working). Ongoing bleeding despite balloon = NEGATIVE test (consider surgical escalation).
Excellent. No bleeding around/through an inflated intrauterine balloon = positive tamponade test = balloon is working. Continue balloon management; avoid unnecessary surgery.
